--- title: "Real Argo Positions on the GLORYS Field" jupyter: python3 fig-dpi: 300 bibliography: ../paper/references.bib execute: cache: false --- ```{=html} ``` The real 2010–2019 Argo profile positions sample the GLORYS12 OHC field, whose box means are known exactly. Each estimator's error is therefore its realized sampling bias for the array that was actually deployed. Field, boxes and depth mask are those of [the simulation report](osim.qmd). # Setup **Field and target.** $Z$ is GLORYS $0$–$2000$ m OHC on the native $1/12^\circ$ grid, daily, on cells deeper than $2000$ m. Let $\mathbb P_{b,m}$ be the normalized area $\times$ time measure on box $b$ and month $m$. The target is the box-month mean $\bar Z_{b,m} = \int Z\,d\mathbb P_{b,m}$, and box-year (or multi-year) values are the day-weighted averages of the months, which equal the mean over all days. Box $A\cup B$ is the area-weighted combination of the two disjoint boxes. **Profiles.** Every Argo fix in $14$–$55^\circ$ N, $72$–$32^\circ$ W from 2010–2019, dropping only fixes within $24$ h of the same float's previous fix (repeat reports of one profile): $62{,}899$ profiles from $813$ floats. Each profile reads $Z$ at its containing cell and day. **Sample mean.** The mean of the box-month's in-box profiles. # Mean field Following @sukianto2026 (their eq. 5), which extends @ridgway2002 and @roemmich2009 with linear and quadratic time trends, the mean field is a local polynomial regression in a fixed square window $\mathcal W(x^*, y^*) = [x^* \pm \lambda] \times [y^* \pm \lambda]$, $\lambda = 5^\circ$, around each centre $(x^*, y^*)$ of a $1^\circ$ grid. It uses all 2010–2019 profiles in the window: $$ \begin{aligned} m_{x^*, y^*}(x, y, t) = {}& \beta_0 + \beta_1 (x - x^*) + \beta_2 (y - y^*) + \beta_3 (x - x^*)(y - y^*) + \beta_4 (x - x^*)^2 + \beta_5 (y - y^*)^2 \\ &+ \sum_{k=1}^{6} \Bigl[\gamma_k \sin\tfrac{2\pi k \tau(t)}{365} + \delta_k \cos\tfrac{2\pi k \tau(t)}{365}\Bigr] + \nu_1 (t - t_D) + \nu_2 (t - t_D)^2, \end{aligned} $$ with $\tau(t)$ the yearday and $t_D$ = 2015-01-01, the midpoint of 2010–2019. The coefficients are ordinary least squares over the window's profiles. The window is never widened: a centre with fewer than $60$ profiles (three per coefficient) is left unfitted. These centres are all over land or shelf outside the boxes. The fit at the centre is $$ \hat\mu(x^*, y^*, t) = \hat\beta_0 + \sum_{k=1}^{6} \Bigl[\hat\gamma_k \sin\tfrac{2\pi k \tau(t)}{365} + \hat\delta_k \cos\tfrac{2\pi k \tau(t)}{365}\Bigr] + \hat\nu_1 (t - t_D) + \hat\nu_2 (t - t_D)^2 . $$ Off the grid, $\hat\mu(x, y, t)$ interpolates the four surrounding centres bilinearly, renormalized over the fitted ones. This is our choice: @sukianto2026 define $\hat\mu$ only at the grid points. The box-month mean of $\hat\mu$ is its integral over $0.5^\circ$ cells at their deep-area centroids and three time nodes per month. For DR, $\hat\mu^{(-f)}$ refits every window without float $f$'s profiles (exactly, by removing that float's contribution to each window's normal equations). # Kriging The anomaly $Z - \hat\mu$ is a zero-mean Gaussian process with the locally stationary anisotropic exponential covariance of @kuusela2018: $$ k\bigl((x, y, t), (x', y', t')\bigr) = \phi \exp(-d) + \sigma^2 \mathbf 1\{\text{same point}\}, \qquad d^2 = \Bigl(\tfrac{x - x'}{\theta_{\text{lon}}}\Bigr)^2 + \Bigl(\tfrac{y - y'}{\theta_{\text{lat}}}\Bigr)^2 + \Bigl(\tfrac{t - t'}{\theta_t}\Bigr)^2, $$ with $(\phi, \theta_{\text{lon}}, \theta_{\text{lat}}, \theta_t, \sigma^2/\phi)$ fixed per $2^\circ$ cell. The parameters are fitted exactly as in [the simulation report](osim.qmd#sec-krige) (window MLE, years as replicates, median over months), but to GLORYS OHC minus a local mean field, on the complete 1° × 10 d lattice of 2015–2019. That makes them **oracle** values: no real analysis has the full field. They were fitted with an earlier version of $\hat\mu$ (2 harmonics, linear trend, widened windows), and their medians differ from fits to GLORYS's own anomaly by only 15–35%. The table gives the medians over cells. | | $\phi$ | $\theta_{\text{lon}}$ | $\theta_{\text{lat}}$ | $\theta_t$ | |---|---|---|---|---| | Box A (median over cells) | 19.4 | 3.5° | 2.9° | 83 d | | Box B (median over cells) | 48.9 | 2.4° | 1.5° | 38 d | Prediction is simple kriging in continuous time: a target in cell $c$ conditions on all profiles within $\pm 10^\circ$ and $\pm 180$ d and uses cell $c$'s parameters. Treating years as independent is a working assumption for fitting the parameters only; the predictor does not block by year. The box-month mean of $\hat\mu + \hat\eta$ uses the same node quadrature as the mean field. # DR kriging With $\hat m^{(-f)}$ the mean-field-plus-kriging map built without float $f$, $\hat q_f$ the expected profile intensity of float $f$ from GLORYS-advected clouds (anchored $\approx 40$ d earlier, with fitted dispersion and speed error) and $\hat Q = \sum_f \hat q_f$, $$ \hat Z_{\text{DR}} = \int \sum_f \frac{\hat q_f}{\hat Q}\,\hat m^{(-f)}\,d\mathbb P_{b,m} \;+\; \frac{1}{\mu(T_{b,m})}\sum_{i} \frac{Z_i - \hat m^{(-f(i))}(x_i, t_i)}{\hat Q(x_i, t_i)}\,\mathbf 1_C(x_i, t_i), $$ on the covered set $C$ (full-data map off it). DR is run for 2015–2019 only; kriging covers 2010–2019, and months in early 2010 can only condition on later profiles because the record starts in January 2010. # Results ::: {#cell-fig-series .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Monthly box-mean OHC (solid) and the box mean of the estimated mean field (dashed), and their difference, the box-mean anomaly the mean field leaves (bottom), 2010-2019, GJ per m2.](glorys_testbed_files/figure-html/fig-series-output-1.png){#fig-series width=1199 height=704} ::: ::: The mean field follows the seasonal cycle and the decade-long warming. What it leaves is interannual and persistent. Box B's monthly anomaly ranges from $-2.0$ to $+3.0$ GJ/m$^2$, and it stays positive through all of 2012 and 2018. Box A's ranges from $-0.8$ to $+1.3$. This is the error a mean field alone carries into each year. ## Bias by box and year Each cell is bias = estimate − truth in GJ/m$^2$, with the bias as a percentage of the truth in brackets. ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Box A

Each panel has its own vertical scale, and DR starts in 2015. ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Yearly, percent of truth ![](glorys_testbed_files/figure-html/cell-5-output-2.png){width=1419 height=924} ### Yearly, GJ per m2 ![](glorys_testbed_files/figure-html/cell-5-output-4.png){width=1419 height=924} ### Monthly, percent of truth ![](glorys_testbed_files/figure-html/cell-5-output-6.png){width=1418 height=924} ### Monthly, GJ per m2 ![](glorys_testbed_files/figure-html/cell-5-output-8.png){width=1428 height=924} ::: ## On the scale of changes and trends OHC is used through its anomalies, year-to-year changes and trends, so a bias matters relative to those, not to the $70$–$80$ GJ/m$^2$ total. Over 2010–2019 the true box-year mean warms by 0\.24 (Box A) and 0\.50 (Box B) GJ/m$^2$ per year. The true and estimated change from the previous year (day-weighted) or month, as GJ/m$^2$ and as a percentage of the previous value; sample mean left, model-based estimators right. Monthly changes include the seasonal cycle. ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Yearly, percent change ![](glorys_testbed_files/figure-html/cell-7-output-2.png){width=1432 height=924} ### Yearly, GJ per m2 ![](glorys_testbed_files/figure-html/cell-7-output-4.png){width=1409 height=924} ### Monthly, percent change ![](glorys_testbed_files/figure-html/cell-7-output-6.png){width=1418 height=924} ### Monthly, GJ per m2 ![](glorys_testbed_files/figure-html/cell-7-output-8.png){width=1418 height=924} ::: - **Sample mean.** Essentially unbiased in Box A (\-0\.06 GJ/m$^2$ over 2010–2019). In Box B it is \-1\.77 GJ/m$^2$ (\-2\.5%) and reaches about $-7\%$ in 2010 and 2016. The floats sit preferentially on the cold side of the Gulf Stream. - **Mean field.** It removes most of Box B's sampling bias (\-0\.29 GJ/m$^2$ over 2010–2019). What remains is the interannual anomaly in the figure above, up to $1.8\%$ in a single year. - **Mean field + kriging.** Over 2010–2019 it has the smallest bias in Box B and in $A\cup B$ (\-0\.17 GJ/m$^2$ in Box B). In Box A it is slightly worse than the sample mean, which has no bias to remove there. Single years still reach $\pm 1.4\%$ in Box B. In 2018, for example, it turns the mean field's $-0.8$ into $+1.0$. - **Mean field + DR kriging.** It does not improve on kriging, and in Box B it adds variance. These are realized errors of one array in one ocean, so year-to-year differences of a few tenths of a GJ/m$^2$ between estimators are within noise.
